belongs_to: 6.1 'This property can be visualised nicely using a diagram' for a (b + c) = ab + ac
description: Two light-green rounded rectangles side by side, each full of gold/mustard filled circles. Above the left one a black square bracket labelled 'b columns' (b blue); above the right one a black bracket labelled 'c columns' (c green). To the left of the left box a tall black bracket labelled 'a rows' (a pink) that spans the full height of the boxes. LEFT box (ab): 5 rows of filled dots are drawn: 3 rows at the top and 2 rows at the bottom, with a gap between them. In every drawn row there are 3 filled dots at the left, then a dotted ellipsis (about 5 small black dots), then 2 filled dots at the right (so 5 filled dots per drawn row). RIGHT box (ac): the same 5 drawn rows (3 at the top, 2 at the bottom), each with 2 filled dots at the left, a dotted ellipsis (about 6 small dots), then 1 filled dot at the right (3 filled dots per drawn row); the 3 filled columns are continued by vertical ellipses of 4 small dots in the gap; the word 'ac' (a pink, c green) in the middle. Under both boxes, centred, the caption 'a (b + c)' (a pink, b blue, c green). The two boxes have the same height; the left box is wider than the right box.
unclear: Number of small dots in each ellipsis is decorative (about 5 horizontal, 4 vertical) and not a stated count.

belongs_to: 6.1 'How do we expand this? ... (a + 1) (b + 1) = (a + 1) b + (a + 1) 1' and the same with a = 23, b = 27 (increase when both numbers are increased by 1)

Four pink curved arrows above line 1: over the first term '(a + 1) b' one arrow runs from a to b and a shorter one from the 1 to b; over the second term '(a + 1) 1' one arrow runs from a to the last 1 and a shorter one from the 1 to the last 1. RIGHT column: the text 'If a = 23, and, b = 27, we get' above, then line 1 '(23 + 1) (27 + 1) = (23 + 1) 27 + (23 + 1) 1', line 2 '= 23 x 27 + [ (27 + 23 + 1) ]' with (27 + 23 + 1) in a black box and 'Increase' under it. The same four pink curved arrows as on the left sit over line 1 (from 23 and from 1 to 27, and from 23 and from 1 to the last 1).

belongs_to: 6.1 'What happens when one of the numbers in a product is increased by 1 and the other is decreased by 1?' expansion of (a + 1) (b - 1) and the 23, 27 case

LEFT column: '(a + 1) (b - 1) = (a + 1) b - (a + 1) 1' / '= ab + b - (a + 1)' / '= ab + [ b - a - 1 ]' with 'b - a - 1' inside a black rectangular box and the word 'Increase' under the box. belongs_to: 6.1 'This identity can be visualised as follows' (a + m) (b + n), blocks ab, an, mb, mn

Top-left block 'ab', top-right block 'an', bottom-left block 'mb', bottom-right block 'mn'. Black square brackets: above the top row, 'b columns' over the left column of blocks (b blue) and 'n columns' over the right column (n green); at the left, 'a rows' (a pink) bracket spanning the height of the top blocks and 'm rows' (m blue) bracket spanning the height of the bottom blocks. The two left blocks are wider than the two right blocks; the two top blocks are taller than the two bottom blocks. DOTS: ab block: 5 rows drawn (3 at the top, 2 at the bottom, gap between), each drawn row = 3 filled dots, dotted ellipsis, 2 filled dots (5 filled per row); vertical ellipses of small dots continue the columns in the gap. an block: 5 rows drawn (3 top, 2 bottom), each row = 2 filled dots, ellipsis, 1 filled dot (3 filled per row), vertical ellipses in the gap. mb block: 3 rows drawn (2 at the top, 1 at the bottom, gap between), each row = 2 filled dots, ellipsis, 2 filled dots (4 filled per row), vertical ellipses in the gap. mn block: 3 rows drawn (2 top, 1 bottom), each row = 2 filled dots, ellipsis, 1 filled dot (3 filled per row), vertical ellipses in the gap. unclear: Purpose of the grey dashed outlines around the first row and first column of each block is not explained in the book text.

belongs_to: 6.2 Try This (p.148): 'Show that (a + b) x (a - b) = a^2 - b^2 geometrically.' -- Hint figure at the top of this page with the text 'What do we get when this piece is moved?'
description: A rectangle drawn in two colours plus an empty dashed strip. Main block: a muted blue (slate-blue) rectangle at the left with a solid black outline on its top and left, and, attached to its right and the same height, a narrower red rectangle (red outline dashed). Under the blue-and-red block a white strip, drawn with a thin grey dashed outline, the same total width as blue + red and short in height; a thin grey dashed vertical line divides it at the same x position as the blue/red boundary, so the strip has a wide left cell under the blue part and a narrow right cell under the red part. Dimension arrows: above the figure a double-headed arrow over the blue width labelled 'a' and a short double-headed arrow over the red width labelled 'b'; at the left a long vertical double-headed arrow, labelled 'a', spanning the whole height (blue block plus the white dashed strip); next to it, at the bottom left, a short vertical double-headed arrow labelled 'b' spanning the height of the white dashed strip. A black curved arrow starts at the right edge of the red rectangle, sweeps down and to the left under the figure, and its arrowhead points up into the white dashed strip (towards its left cell), meaning the red piece is moved there. Text at the right of the arc: 'What do we get when this piece is moved?'. So: blue + red = (a + b) wide and (a - b) tall; the white strip below is b tall.

belongs_to: 6.3 Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake: 'We have expanded and simplified some algebraic expressions below ... Check each of the simplifications and see if there is a mistake.' (cards 1-12)
description: A board of 12 rounded rectangles with amber/gold borders, arranged 4 rows x 3 columns, each with a small black-outlined numbered circle badge on its top-left corner (numbers 1-12 row by row). Text inside each (italic maths, as printed): 1: -3p (-5p + 2q) / = -3p + 5p - 2q / = p - 2q. 2: 2(x - 1) + 3(x + 4) / = 2x - 1 + 3x + 4 / = 5x + 3. 3: y + 2 (y + 2) / = (y + 2)^2 / = y^2 + 4y + 4. 4: (5m + 6n)^2 / = 25m^2 + 36n^2. 5: (-q + 2)^2 / = q^2 - 4q + 4. 6: 3a (2b x 3c) / = 6ab x 9ac / = 54a2bc (printed as '54a2bc', the 2 not raised). 7: (1/2) (10s - 6) + 3 / = 5s - 3 + 3 / = 5s (fraction 1/2 printed stacked). 8: 5w^2 + 6w / = 11w^2. 9: 2a^3 + 3a^3 + 6a^2b / + 6ab^2 / = 5a^3 + 12a^2b^2. 10: (x + 2)(x + 5) / = (x + 2)x + (x + 2)5 / = x^2 + 2x + 5x + 10 / = x^2 + 7x + 10. 11: (a + 2) (b + 4) / = ab + 8. 12: ab^2 + a^2b + a^2b^2 / = ab (a + b + ab).
unclear: Card 6 last line is printed '54a2bc' (superscript missing); card 9 first expression wraps onto two lines (the '+ 6ab^2' on the second line).
